title: Generative AI Exercises
description: Practise the ideas from this Generative AI course. Each answer has an explanation to help you learn.

exercises.question: What should happen after receiving generated text?
exercises.explanation: Generative AI creates an output using patterns learned during training. It can produce a new sentence or picture, but the result still needs checking. This is a written example of a possible output. It shows what we would check; the website has not called a text model.

exercises.question: Which stage changes the learned model numbers?
exercises.explanation: Training changes a model using examples. Generation uses an already prepared model to produce an output. Asking a question is not the same operation as retraining all its weights. These are different stages with different costs and purposes. A service may have its own data policies, so read those before sharing information.

exercises.question: Why does this code choose flies?
options: It has the highest supplied score
The code saw a real kite
exercises.explanation: A language model predicts possible next pieces of text. This tiny list only illustrates choosing a next word; it is not a trained language model. The output is The kite flies. max finds the pair with the largest hand-written score. [0] then selects its word.

exercises.question: What is wrong with the 7 AM claim?
exercises.explanation: A model can produce a believable statement that is false. This is often called a hallucination. Smooth writing is not evidence that a fact is correct. The claim fills a gap with an unsupported time. A careful answer should identify the missing information or use a trustworthy source.

exercises.question: Which detail is supported?
exercises.explanation: Grounding means tying an answer to supplied evidence. The answer should stay within what that evidence supports. The answer uses the day stated in the source. It does not guess a time because no time appears there.

exercises.question: Which instruction describes a visible subject?
exercises.explanation: A picture request should describe the subject, setting and useful visual details. A model may miss a detail, so inspect the image afterward. The plan names visible features that can be checked. It does not claim that an image has been generated.

exercises.question: What does this simplified generation start from?
exercises.explanation: Many image models use diffusion. In a simplified view, generation starts with noise and repeatedly changes it toward a picture guided by a request. This is a concept sketch. Real systems use numeric representations and a chosen schedule of steps; they do not reveal a ready-made picture hidden in noise.

exercises.question: What should a timer sound review include?
exercises.explanation: Generated audio may include speech, music or effects. A useful request names the length and purpose so the result can fit its setting. The plan makes duration and comfort part of the review. It describes an example request and does not create or play audio.

exercises.question: Why test an empty list?
options: It is a useful edge case
exercises.explanation: Code from a model is a proposed solution. Read it and check examples, including small edge cases, before using it. The outputs are 5 and 0. The empty-list check matters because a function can work on a normal case and still fail on an edge case.

exercises.question: How should two candidates be compared?
exercises.explanation: Some generation methods choose among several possible outputs. A seed can help repeat a run, but exact repeatability also depends on tools and settings. Both candidates could fit the request. The review criteria matter more than receiving the same answer every time.

exercises.question: Which is a factual check?
options: The explanation of water drops is accurate
The title uses a bright colour
exercises.explanation: Evaluation is a planned check of the result. Include the task rules and the mistakes that would matter to the user. The checks separate writing quality from factual accuracy. A friendly tone does not replace a correct explanation.

exercises.question: Who checks the final poster before sharing?
exercises.explanation: Before sharing generated work, review facts, privacy, permissions and suitability. Keep a person responsible for the final choice. The checklist connects review to a specific poster. It does not replace the publisher's rules or the rights of source creators.
